What are some tips and good measures for first time Tattoo receivers?

Relax, it won't be as bad as you expect.

Also, eat something first.

Also, eat something first.

Is this because you will sit there for awhile or something to do with your skin?

If your blood sugar levels are low, you may feel dizzy or faint when you're being tattooed. This can happen even if you don't have a blood sugar disorder. It won't happen to everyone, but especially if you've never been tattooed before it's best to play it safe and have a sandwich or something before your appointment.

• Don't drink any alcohol beforehand - It thins your blood, which makes you bleed more.
  • Eat before you go - keeps you from getting woozy while being tattooed.
  • Choose an artist that has a portfolio that jives with the style you want
  • (assuming the previous) Give the artist leeway to be an artist - They do it for a living, you'll get better results if you take their advice.
  • Make sure you tip the artist
  • Don't be afraid to ask for a break - they're charging by the hour and it's your money, if you need 5-15 minutes, just ask.
  • never ask for a cheaper price than the original quote - it just means they'll have to rush through it or cut corners, not a good idea for something that will be on your body for the rest of your life.
  • If they ain't wearing gloves or you didn't see the needles come out of sterile packaging ABORT
The tipping part only counts in countries where tipping applies though, everything else is spot on.
"Never ask for a cheaper price"...... More likely you'll just piss off the tattooist. And do you really want to start on a bad note with someone who's going to be sticking needles in you?...

Eat beforehand and if it is a big tattoo, bring some trail mix with you. Also, if you know you will be lying down, bring a small pillow or hoodie to rest on. Don't psych yourself out because it's not going to hurt as bad as you think it will. Also, wear appropriate clothing. If you are getting tattooed on your leg, wear shorts. If on your ribs/sternum/back pasties are always a great option for girls! That way you don't have to do the awkward taping a paper towel to your breasts thing. And make sure to tip your artist afterwards!
I want a large rib piece that will be my first tattoo...I'm assuming it will probably hurt more than I think....

It's going to hurt no matter what, but sometimes people (especially first timers) tend to psych themselves out so much it makes it worse. You might be surprised at how well you handle it. When I got my foot tattooed (like, the entire top of the foot) I thought it was going to be awful but I was pleasantly surprised at how easy it was for me. Everyone's pain tolerance is different for different areas, so don't stress! Good luck :)

I got a piano keyboard on my ribcage as my first tattoo. Because of the straight lines he had to go very very slow and deep and it took over 3 hours. The ribcage is one of the most painful spots to get tattooed but all I can say is try not to move and talk to your artist. They are used to distracting people from pain and in my experience they love to talk to you while they're working. Like others have said in this thread, bring a snack and take a break. Stand up, walk around a bit, take some deep breaths, then get back on the table. Once you've started you can't really stop so you just have to make that initial commitment. I always have this thought like, "WHY THE FUCK DID I DECIDE TO DO THIS TO MYSELF" the second it starts because, yeah, it hurts. But ultimately it's not the worst and it's worth it
